# nominee

Authorize the action, not the agent. nominee enforces user-aware policy at the tool boundary, resolves credentials at execution time, and keeps tamper-evident proof. Framework-neutral, zero dependencies in the core.

Agent frameworks already provide useful approval, guardrail, and durable resume primitives. nominee complements them when a tool decision must incorporate application user/resource authorization, exact-input binding, call-time credentials, narrowing delegation, or one evidence stream across runtimes.

nominee sits in-process between the model and tools. Every tool call is checked against declarative allow/deny/ask policy; official wrappers reject input changed after authorization; decisions are sealed into a hash-chained receipt log; and tools can resolve fresh, scope-separated user credentials at call time.

Layers: your agent/framework (AI SDK, Eve, Mastra, Cloudflare, MCP, standalone) → nominee (policy, approvals, receipts, tokens) → your vault/store (env, DB, OAuth2, Auth0 Token Vault, Supabase).

Key concepts:
- **Policy**: ordered `allow` / `deny` / `ask` rules over tool calls. Glob tool-name patterns (`github.*`), argument-level `when` predicates, call budgets (`max`), and a `fallback` effect (default `ask`). First match wins. The model cannot talk its way past a deny — `PolicyDeniedError` is thrown before the tool runs.
- **guard()**: `nominee.guard(tools, { user })` wraps a whole tools object so every call is authorized and its input fingerprint is re-checked immediately before execution. Manual `authorize(...)` integrations call `await assertUnchanged(authorization, input)` before executing. `check(...)` is a side-effect-free dry run.
- **Approvals**: `ask` rules (and `nominee.approve({ user, action })`) block until a human decides — via `onApprovalRequest` + `req.approve()/req.deny()`, a webhook calling `nominee.resolveApproval(id, 'approved')`, or natively via a strategy like Auth0 CIBA. Denials throw `ApprovalDeniedError`.
- **Receipts**: every decision, approval, and token grant appends to a hash chain (optional HMAC signing key). `delivery: 'strict'` waits for an async external sink before an allowed async operation returns; buffered sinks expose `flushReceipts()`. Durable agents can pass `resume: { seq, prev }` to continue a chain.
- **Delegation**: `nominee.delegate('sub-agent', { policy })` — the strictest outcome across the chain wins (deny > ask > allow); a sub-agent can only narrow authority, and its receipts carry the full chain `user → orchestrator → sub-agent`.
- **Tokens** (supporting act): agents request `nominee.token({ user, connection, scopes })` at call time. Cache and single-flight keys include the canonical scope set. Strategies swap the backing store (plain function, OAuth2, Auth0 Token Vault, Supabase) without touching agent code.
- **Adapters**: `nominee-ai` (Vercel AI SDK + Cloudflare Agents: `guardTools`, `nomineeTool`), `nominee-eve` (Vercel Eve: `nomineeTool`). Core `guard()` covers Mastra, OpenAI Agents, MCP, and anything with `{ execute }`.

Runnable proof: a prompt-injected agent tries to exfiltrate email and is blocked by policy before the tool runs, with a signed receipt of the attempt — https://github.com/bharath31/nominee/tree/main/examples/prompt-injection-blocked (no API keys). Live version: https://nominee.dev/agent runs the same block for real, inside a Cloudflare Durable Object that hibernates mid-session and resumes the same receipt chain when it wakes. Token-freshness proof (naive rotating refresh fails 7/8 under concurrency; nominee 8/8): https://github.com/bharath31/nominee/tree/main/examples/token-refresh-correctness

When you DON'T need nominee: a read-only agent with no authority worth guarding; a platform whose native permission system covers you end-to-end; or you want one fully-managed vendor for tools + auth + policy (use Arcade or Composio directly).

## Quick Start
```typescript
import { Nominee, allow, deny, ask } from 'nominee'

const nominee = new Nominee({
  policy: {
    rules: [
      allow('email.read'),
      allow('email.forward', { when: ({ input }) => input.to.endsWith('@acme.com') }),
      deny('email.forward', { reason: 'external forwarding is exfiltration' }),
      ask('email.delete'),
    ],
    fallback: 'deny',
  },
  onApprovalRequest: (req) => req.approve(), // wire to Slack / push / your UI
})

const tools = nominee.guard({ 'email.read': readEmail, 'email.forward': forwardEmail }, { user: 'alice' })
// Denied calls throw PolicyDeniedError before the tool runs; every outcome is on nominee.receipts.
```

Docs: https://nominee.dev/docs/ · GitHub: https://github.com/bharath31/nominee · npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/nominee
